ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, ss 5 (definition of beneficial owner), 10 (risk assessment), 14-18 (customer due diligence), 31-33 (record-keeping); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2011, rr 5-10; Companies Act 1993, ss 87-89 (substantial shareholder disclosure) and Part 8 (share registers); no public UBO register exists in New Zealand; the AML/CFT supervisors (Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs) and the Financial Intelligence Unit retain full access rights to UBO records upon lawful request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration and source-of-wealth statement (including a summary of funds used for capitalization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the New Zealand Police / FMA PEP list; (ii) the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctions list pursuant to the United Nations Act 1946, the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, and the Iran, North Korea, and Myanmar sanctions regulations; (iii) the OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions; and (iv) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is automatically triggered for any PEP, family member, or close associate of a PEP, and at any occurrence of an adverse media hit, prior criminal financial conduct, or transaction inconsistency. Screening must be repeated at least annually and before each high-value payment run.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (NZ Companies Register) - online name reservation module at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may use English and Maori words; the registered name must be entered in Latin script. The Registrar disregards punctuation, diacritics, and macrons when comparing similarity of names. Where a name is desired in non-Latin script (e.g., Mandarin characters), the applicant must file a Latin-script transliteration and may reserve the transliterated name only; the non-Latin name cannot appear on the official register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying Crown or government connection: 'Crown', 'Government', 'Royal', 'Ministerial'
Entity form suffixes: 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'Charitable Trust' unless the entity's legal form actually possesses that designation
Terms regulated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013: 'Bank', 'Building Society', 'Insurance', 'Broker', 'Finance'
Terms restricted under the Flags, Emblems, and Names Protection Act 1981: 'Anzac', the New Zealand flag, royal names
Maori terms of cultural significance (e.g., 'Tarai', 'Kingitanga') requiring prior consultation with the Ministry of Maori Development
Words likely to mislead or cause offence, or implying a connection with a public authority or the armed forces
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reservation expires at the end of 20 working days (the Companies Act 1993 s 22(3)); no administrative extension exists, and a fresh application with payment is required after expiry. On rejection, the applicant may (1) request a written statement of reasons from the Registrar; (2) submit a formal administrative review application within 20 working days of the rejection notice to the National Manager, New Zealand Companies Office, attaching a concise submission distinguishing the proposed name from existing identical or confusingly similar names and addressing each objection; (3) if the administrative review is denied, file for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 20 working days of the denial, seeking certiorari or a declaration. All time limits run from receipt of the written notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible, subject to s 200 of the Companies Act 1993: the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand, open during ordinary business hours, and serve as the place for delivery of legal process and regulatory notices. A virtual office provider or registered agent offering a physical presence, a street address, and an on-site representative who accepts documents satisfies the statutory test. P.O. Box addresses are prohibited. For a non-standard commercial activity such as a cross-border consumer polling SaaS platform, a serviced office or registered agent address is acceptable provided the agent agrees to forward all documents without delay.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 5% annual probability) for a low-risk, fully digital market-research company under the AML/CFT risk-based supervision of the FMA/DIA; however, targeted inspections can occur without warning if any of the following arise: abnormal payment flows through PayPal or Wise, repeated small-amount payouts to personal accounts, sanctions-list matches, or inconsistencies in UBO declarations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (1993 No 105), New Zealand, particularly Part 2 'Incorporation and De-registration' (ss. 12-21), s. 10 'Simultaneous registration', ss. 22-31 'Name requirements', ss. 84-87 'Share registers', ss. 126-135 'Directors' duties', ss. 150-160 'Board and appointment of officers', and Schedule 1 'Constitution'. Supporting statutes: Financial Reporting Act 2013, Income Tax Act 2007, Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, Privacy Act 2020, and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2024.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Tari Kamupene o Aotearoa), a functional agency of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Act 1993 Form 2 / NZCN), filed electronically through the Companies Office Online Register; the granted application operates as the Certificate of Incorporation and issues a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 prescribes no minimum issued or paid-up capital, no nominal-capital requirement, and no escrow or pre-incorporation deposit obligation. A company must allot at least one ordinary share and have at least one shareholder, and at least one director must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand (s. 150). Consideration for issued shares may take any lawful form, including cash, property, or services; unpaid capital may remain unsubscribed until commercial need arises, which is compatible with the low-risk digital SaaS operating model.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
MINUTES OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (THE 'COMPANY'), HELD AT 10:00 A.M. NEW ZEALAND STANDARD TIME ON [●], AT THE COMPANY'S REGISTERED OFFICE, PURSUANT TO THE COMPANIES ACT 1993.

MEMBERS PRESENT: [Names of directors] (together, the 'Board').

NOTICE AND QUORUM: The chairman confirmed that due notice of the meeting had been given to every director in accordance with s. 152 of the Companies Act 1993 and that a quorum was present throughout.

The chairman presented the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office (Company Number [●]) and the NZBN confirmation notice, and the Board transacted the following business.

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED that the Company issue and allot to the subscribers named in the Application for Registration of a Company a total of [●] ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, fully paid as to par value by cash, property, or services-in-kind in accordance with the respective Share Subscription Agreements; that the share register of the Company be updated forthwith in accordance with s. 84 of the Companies Act 1993; and that the directors be and are hereby authorised to issue share certificates to the allottees.

2. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Reservation, and NZBN Pre-Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Register (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free search of the New Zealand company and trade-name register to confirm that the proposed name (e.g., '[Group] Consumer Survey Platform Limited') is available, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name, does not contain a restricted word (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'National', 'University') requiring ministerial consent, and ends with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Reserve the approved name online at no charge for up to 20 working days to secure it during the incorporation application. Run an NZBN directory check to confirm no conflicting legal entity holds the intended NZBN or trade identity.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to three alternatives)
Applicant identity details (individual or corporate)
Name availability search record retained as evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines the name under ss. 22-24 of the Companies Act 1993 (e.g., misleading similarity or restricted word), the applicant may file an online administrative review request within 5 working days or immediately reserve a corrected alternative name. A persisting refusal may be appealed in writing to the Registrar under s. 377 of the Companies Act 1993; no additional governmental fee is chargeable for the reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Application, Statutory Consents, and Beneficial Ownership Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Statutory Compliance Section (pre-filing submission file)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the statutory incorporation pack ahead of electronic lodgment: the proposed company name, a physical registered-office address in New Zealand (street address, not a P.O. Box), an address for service, at least one director ordinarily resident in New Zealand, subscriber/shareholder particulars, and either a bespoke company constitution or the Schedule 1 default constitution. Each proposed director and shareholder must execute a formal consent to act (ss. 151 and 156, Companies Act 1993). For foreign signatories, have the consent forms witnessed by a notary public and the identity documents certified where the Registrar requires identity verification. Prepare in draft the beneficial-ownership register identifying every natural person with 25% or more control of the company, so that the disclosure obligations of the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2024 can be met immediately upon request.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company (Form 2 draft)
Signed consent-to-act form for each proposed director (s. 151)
Signed consent-to-act form for each subscriber/shareholder (s. 156)
Company constitution (bespoke or adoption of Schedule 1 default)
For foreign signatories: notarized passport copy and proof of residential address
Beneficial-ownership register template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a s. 14 deficiency letter regarding incomplete consents, invalid registered-office address, or inconsistent capital particulars, counsel may respond in writing within 5 working days with corrective documentation. Where the query concerns missing notarization of a foreign signature, the signatory may present the original notarized instrument to a New Zealand embassy or recognized notary, file the certified copy electronically, and processing resumes without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Application and Payment of Statutory Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Company Register Portal (operated under MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Office online register using a RealMe-verified individual login or the myNZBN corporate credential; select the 'Register a Company' workflow; import the pre-drafted Form 2 data; attach the executed director and shareholder consents and the constitution; certify the beneficial-ownership declarations; and pay the statutory incorporation fee of NZ$150 via Visa, Mastercard, or direct debit. The platform automatically performs availability and identity checks; upon approval by the Registrar, the system allocates the company number and NZBN and releases the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Complete Form 2 data filed online
Executed consent-to-act documents attached as PDF
Company constitution (if bespoke) attached in the filing bundle
Proof of payment of the NZ$150 filing fee
RealMe-verified applicant credential
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the online application is rejected with a deficiency code (e.g., 'Director consent missing', 'Name not distinctive', 'Address invalid'), the filer may correct the fields and resubmit within 10 working days without paying a second filing fee. If the Registrar refuses registration on substantive grounds under s. 18 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may submit written representations to the Registrar within 15 working days, and the Registrar must issue a decision within a further 5 working days, with right of appeal to the High Court thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN, convene the first board meeting to adopt the constitution (if not already adopted), allot the subscribed shares, appoint the directors and company secretary, confirm the registered office, and authorize the opening of corporate bank and payment accounts. Establish the statutory registers at the registered office or on an approved electronic register platform: the share register (s. 84), the directors and officers register (s. 87), the beneficial-ownership register (as amended by the 2024 Act), and the minute book. Issue executed share certificates to each subscriber and, where an overseas parent exists, file the Register of Ultimate Holding Company (s. 98) within 10 working days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation letter
Share certificates and share register ledger
Original signed consent-to-act forms placed in the corporate minute book
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors (company name, company number, or incorporation date), lodge an administrative correction request through the Companies Office online service within 5 working days; corrected certificates are reissued within 2 working days at no cost. Deficiencies in beneficial-ownership records may be cured by an internal rectification resolution and evidenced to the Registrar if a verification notice is served under the beneficial-ownership regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD Number, GST, PAYE, and Foreign Supplier Compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) New Zealand - Business Registration Portal (MyIR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first month after incorporation, complete the IRD business registration through MyIR using the NZBN and incorporation details; the IRD number is issued online. Determine GST status under s. 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985: registration is compulsory if taxable supplies exceed NZ$60,000 in any 12-month period; the platform may elect voluntary GST registration immediately to recover input tax on SaaS infrastructure costs. If the entity will employ staff in New Zealand, effect PAYE and employer KiwiSaver registration. Because the business will make mass payouts to panel members through PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, prepare the AML/CFT customer-due-diligence file for recipients and confirm compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 on the IRD business questionnaire.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN number
Online IR342 (IRD Business Registration) application
Voluntary GST registration election (GST 1) if desired
PAYE/employer registration form if the company has employees
Ultimate beneficial-owner details for the exchange of information (CRS) purposes
AML/CFT due-diligence statements covering the mass-payout beneficiary list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue delays or queries the registration (commonly on missing overseas beneficial-ownership detail), the taxpayer may respond in MyIR with the Companies Office extract and a statutory declaration within 10 working days. Where the IRD number was not issued timeously, the IRD may backdate the effective date of registration on written application under s. 111 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, subject to disclosure of all relevant facts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Privacy Governance, Data-Protection Appointments, and Workplace Safety Clearance for Business Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); and the relevant local Territorial Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As the consumer-panel survey platform collects personal data from respondents in New Zealand and offshore, implement Privacy Act 2020 compliance: appoint a Privacy Officer, publish a privacy statement describing collection, use, cross-border transfer, and retention practices, and establish the notifiable-breach reporting procedure and internal complaints mechanism. Execute data-processing schedules with PayPal and Wise governing transfers of panel-member payment data. For any leased office, verify that the building holds a current building warrant of fitness and, if 10 or more persons are employed, register an approved fire-evacuation scheme with FENZ. Finalize the hazard register and health-and-safety induction documentation required by the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and display the H&S policy notice at the workplace before staff commence duties.
required_dossiers: Privacy Officer appointment letter
Published privacy policy compliant with the Privacy Act 2020
Notifiable privacy breach response and incident management plan
Building warrant of fitness (BWOF) and Form 12A fire-evacuation approval for the office premises
Health-and-safety hazard register and emergency procedures
Data-processing agreements with PayPal and Wise as payment contractors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Privacy Commissioner issues a compliance notice for inadequate disclosure, the company may submit a written remediation plan within 10 working days to avoid formal enforcement. For a fire-safety infringement notice, remedy the defect and obtain re-inspection within 10 working days from the territorial authority; an excessive penalty may be appealed to the District Court under ss. 167-169 of the Building Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industry-specific licensing board is applicable to ISIC 7320 (market research and opinion polling). General regulatory oversight for the electronic survey platform is exercised by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) for consumer data practices and, where physical premises are established, by the local Territorial Authority for building and fire-safety consent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None. Consumer polling and cross-border market-research SaaS platforms are not designated as licensed occupations or activities under New Zealand sectoral licensing statutes; therefore no operating or manufacturing permit is required. The company's authoritative business dossiers comprise the NZBN certificate, the IRD number, and, where applicable, the GST registration confirmation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no registration or full EIA report is triggered because the consumer-panel platform is a data-services activity with no physical industrial plant, no wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, no hazardous-waste generation, and no land disturbance. Consequently, no resource consent is required under the Resource Management Act 1991 and no EIA scoping under Schedule 4 of that Act applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at formation. If the operator later installs dedicated server rooms, compliance would be limited to municipal wastewater discharge standards under the local council's district plan, e-waste recycling under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, and electrical installation compliance with AS/NZS 3000:2018 as verified by a licensed electrician; no atmospheric discharge or volatile organic compound thresholds are engaged by the standard SaaS workload.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: any New Zealand office premises must hold a current building warrant of fitness (BWOF) evidencing compliance with the Building Act 2004 and the Fire Safety and Evacuation of Buildings Regulations 2006; workplaces with 10 or more employees require an approved fire-evacuation scheme issued by Fire and Emergency New Zealand. Structural Load Inspection: the territorial authority's consents and BWOF records constitute the evidence of structural sufficiency for the occupied floors. Workplace Clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand jurisdiction applies under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; the company must complete a general risk assessment, appoint a health and safety representative, and maintain the H&S policy and hazard register before onboarding staff. No hazardous-substance location approval, dangerous-goods licence, or environmental operating permit is required for the data-driven consumer-panel business model.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) of New Zealand; administrative portal: myIR (www.ird.govt.nz); legislative authority under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (IC) obtains a New Zealand IRD number by filing Form IR742 (Application for an IRD number – Non-Resident Individual or Company) with the Inland Revenue Department, either directly or through an approved New Zealand tax agent. Supplementary GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 is effected separately via Form IR356 or online through myIR when the IC carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or makes supplies of remote services to New Zealand-resident consumers. No statutory licence, minimum capital, or local physical presence is required for registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: For New Zealand tax purposes, the International Company is default-classified as a non-resident company subject to entity-level taxation only on New Zealand-sourced income (notably non-resident withholding tax on NZ interest, dividends, and royalties). All foreign-sourced business income derived by the consumer-panel survey platform falls outside New Zealand's income tax net under the territorial sourcing rules, provided the company is not deemed tax-resident in New Zealand under the dual-residency tie-breaker test and does not have a New Zealand fixed establishment. The classification therefore operates as an offshore tax-exempt zone in respect of the platform's worldwide non-NZ income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' entity election. The relevant statutory election mechanisms are: (i) GST grouping election under section 55 of the GST Act 1985 for related entities; (ii) election of GST accounting basis (payments/cash basis vs. invoice basis) and filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly); (iii) election to register the IC as a New Zealand foreign trust pursuant to the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 where the trust-structured IC has a non-resident settlor, thereby exempting non-NZ-source income; and (iv) hybrid-mismatch elective alignment or self-correction adjustments to neutralise deductible-payment mismatches across cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of cumulative taxable supplies in any 12-month period; registration is compulsory once the threshold is exceeded and voluntary below it for persons carrying on a taxable activity. Non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services to New Zealand-resident consumers are also required to register under the offshore remote-services GST regime once the same NZD 60,000 threshold is met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no API tax-stamping requirement, and no mandatory electronic invoicing for private-sector suppliers. E-invoicing is optional and operates on the Peppol network under the New Zealand e-Invoicing scheme administered by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment; central government agencies are required to receive e-invoices, but suppliers may issue paper or PDF invoices. GST compliance is audited through periodic returns filed in myIR, and the Inland Revenue Department may require SAF-T data extraction as part of an audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available to the consumer-panel survey platform under section 11 of the GST Act 1985 where: (i) goods are physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply; (ii) services are supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and is not in New Zealand when the services are received; or (iii) services are supplied directly to a non-resident business in connection with that business's tax assessment, tax collection, or tax payment obligations (deemed zero-rated B2B supply). Cloud-based market-research and consumer-polling services provided to offshore clients qualify as zero-rated supplies of services when the recipient is outside New Zealand and the services are not performed in connection with land or goods situated in New Zealand. The zero-rating claim must be supported by contemporaneous evidence of the non-resident recipient, the offshore supply nexus, and the receipt of consideration in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Export Entry filed through the New Zealand Trade Single Window or equivalent electronic declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of goods from New Zealand, where goods are exported
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency from the offshore client
Signed commercial invoice and underlying service contract identifying the non-resident recipient and the offshore market-research service
Recipient non-residency certificate or comparable proof of offshore status for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department scrutinises zero-rating claims through document-matching and risk-rating algorithms. An unjustified zero-rating claim triggers a reassessment with GST clawback plus interest from the due date of the return. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 scale by culpability: 20% shortfall penalty for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for a tax-avoidance arrangement, and 150% for evasion or an abusive tax position. Misdeclaration in connection with income tax carries an additional 43% accuracy penalty. Although New Zealand does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, the 180-day benchmark is used by IRD as a reasonable period for receipt of export proceeds; overdue repatriation will be treated as evidence that the export supply is not genuine, leading to cancellation of zero-rating, reversal of input credits, and clawback of refunds. Criminal conviction for export-fraud can result in a fine of up to NZD 250,000 and/or five years' imprisonment per offence, with no time limitation for fraudulent evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. New Zealand operates an open capital account with no exchange-control licensing, no prior approval for profit repatriation, and no limits on dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders, subject only to normal tax withholding obligations (non-resident withholding tax) and AML/CFT scrutiny. Direct inward investment above statutory thresholds may require consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2008, but this is an ownership-control filter, not a currency convertibility restriction. The International Company structure is tax-exempt in its formation jurisdiction; no New Zealand thin capitalization or exchange-control impediments apply to the clearing rails described.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no mandatory surrender of foreign currency to the Reserve Bank, and no minimum conversion ratio. The International Company may retain earnings in offshore foreign-currency accounts and repatriate or settle trade obligations freely via any registered bank or authorised non-bank clearing provider.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High, with structural limits. Cross-border digital EMI/fintech platforms such as Wise and Airwallex can be onboarded as client accounts and payment-disbursement rails, but they are not a regulated bank substitute in New Zealand. Wise holds a New Zealand FSPR licence; Airwallex holds an FSPR registration and operates through partnerships to provide NZD and FX clearing. Neither platform provides the regulated status of a locally incorporated registered bank, and the International Company must still maintain at least one operational banking relationship for escrow, collateral, and large-value settlements. New Zealand does not prohibit offshore EMIs from servicing non-resident International Companies, but the EMI must comply with New Zealand AML/CFT and the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 when carrying on financial services in or from New Zealand.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by directors is not a statutory requirement under New Zealand law. Banks and fintechs use risk-based AML/CFT identity verification; remote onboarding is permissible when supported by tamper-evident identity proof, biometric verification, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and certified corporate custody-chain documents. In practice, for an International Company with non-resident directors, most tier-1 banks require either a secure video interview plus independently notarized corporate documents, or a physical banker's verification appointment at a recognized branch or embassy if the bank's internal risk policy demands it. The mandate therefore is: remote first, but documentary certification and video identity verification are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership of the International Company is obscured by nominee shareholders or bearer-share arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide registered agent certificate of corporate incumbency, full UBO declaration naming each natural-person beneficiary, notarized trust deed and deed of retirement of any nominee shareholder, current register of directors, and sworn source-of-wealth statement for each settlor or beneficiary, accompanied by independent legal opinion confirming the absence of bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trust or International Company jurisdiction is perceived as a high-risk or poorly tax-transparent zone with no automatic exchange of information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit current tax-residency certificate, evidence of CRS/FATCA registration and filing history, the trust and company constitutional documents, a commercial-purpose narrative explaining the cross-border survey platform activity, and annual audited financial statements supported by a licensed auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty exposure from consumer-panel incentive payout rails (mass payments) triggers adverse-media and sanctions screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a documented sanctions and PEP screening policy, PCI-DSS-compliant payout vendor contracts, participant terms and conditions, list of prohibited jurisdictions, and a transaction-monitoring segregation report identifying sampling panel payouts separately from treasury settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intended payment rails (PayPal Mass Payout and Wise) are viewed by the onboarding bank as unverified transaction channels for cross-border outflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed service agreements with Wise and PayPal, API endpoint security certification, evidence of the digital EMI licensing or registration in relevant jurisdictions, expected monthly volume and transaction-size forecasts, historical settlement statements, and the platform's withdrawal and refund workflow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loans into the New Zealand banking platform should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with explicit remitter and beneficiary identification, using the receiving bank's transaction-purpose and narrative classification, such as paid-in capital, shareholder loan, service revenue, or intercompany settlement. New Zealand does not mandate regulatory purpose-code approval, but the receiving bank will require a capital-introduction letter, board resolution, invoiced or subscription documentation, and a UBO diagram. The funds should be held first in a segregated Capital Escrow Account, then moved to the Operational Account only after satisfactory KYC, for the purpose of purchasing panel data, paying software-infrastructure costs, and funding operating expenses.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements should be split by rail: (a) bank-to-bank B2B supplier payments, software licensing, and market-research vendor payments through SWIFT MT103 over the New Zealand clearing system via the tier-1 bank; (b) high-frequency small-value consumer-panel incentives through Wise or PayPal Mass Payout platforms with aggregate settlement by the treasury to the EMI's master account; (c) commercial letter of credit or SWIFT MT700 only for goods-related procurements, although the survey platform's service-based nature will rarely require LC terms. All outbound disbursements are unrestricted under New Zealand FX controls, but must respect applicable sanctions screening and New Zealand AML/CFT record-keeping and verification requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX spot and OTC forward contracts booked with New Zealand registered banks such as ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac, or Kiwibank for up to 12 months, without an ISDA requirement if internally cross-collateralized.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for NZD and emerging-market currency pairs that lack deliverable liquidity, executable via licensed New Zealand or offshore counterparty under Financial Markets Authority conduct rules.
Cross-currency swaps matched to projected multi-scheme survey-panel revenue streams and operating liabilities, documented under ISDA and subject to the bank's credit approval.
Limited vanilla FX options purchased for downside protection on large repatriable dividend or licensing payments, with no leverage and full collateral coverage in the operational settlement account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (confirmation of company name, NZBN, registered office, address for service, directors, shareholders and ultimate holding company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the annual return date (anniversary of incorporation unless the registered annual return date has been changed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under Companies Act 1993, s 218, punishable by fine up to NZ$50,000; overdue status is recorded; continued non-filing results in Registrar's 15-working-day removal notice and administrative strike-off from the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (GPFS) and statutory report, if the company is a reporting entity, 'large' company, or 'large overseas-owned' company under Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) and External Reporting Board (XRB) standards setter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after balance date for companies required to file under FRA 2013; FMC reporting entities must comply with Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 periodic-disclosure deadlines. Small/medium non-reporting companies are exempt from filing and need only prepare accounts as required by shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver financial statements is an offence under s 8/48 of FRA 2013 with fine up to NZ$50,000; continued breach can trigger enforcement action, further pecuniary penalties for FMC reporting entities, and negative registry status impairing ongoing incorporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (IR4/IR10) and any annual non-resident supplementary return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 7 July following the end of the standard 31 March balance date (or, if tax agent has an extension, by 31 March or 31 July for due dates with extension) for a standard balance-date taxpayer; for non-resident exempt-zone entities, nil-return filing requirements still apply if required by IRD assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties commence automatically (NZ$50 minimum for each late return plus interest on unpaid amounts), late payment interest under IRD Act continues; persistent non-filing may lead to default tax assessments and enforcement through the District Court/IRD debt collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory for: (1) FMC reporting entities under Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (2) 'large' companies under FRA 2013 (assets ≥ NZ$60m or revenue ≥ NZ$30m in each of two consecutive accounting periods); (3) 'large overseas-owned' companies carrying on business in New Zealand and exceeding the FRA 2013 thresholds; and (4) any company if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights validly request an audit under Companies Act 1993, s 199. This consumer-panel/SaaS platform, if classified as a small/medium non-reporting entity, is not compulsorily audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Tier 1: NZ IFRS; Tier 2: NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); Small/Medium non-reporting companies: XRB-specified New Zealand GAAP simplified standards. Accounting principles derive from Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not have a public UBO register, but the directors must identify each shareholder and director in the Annual Return each year. The appointed registered office/agent acts as a reporting entity under AML/CFT Act 2009 and must collect, verify, and periodically refresh the beneficial ownership and control data of the company. Any shareholding transfer during the year requires director approval per the constitution, entry in the Register of Members, and notification to the agent so the next annual confirmation cycle reflects current owners/beneficial owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' resolutions and meetings)
Register of Charges (if any secured/registered charges exist)
Share Transfer Register (if any transfers have occurred)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – 1,200 per annum for a registered office and registered agent in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 15,000 for a small-to-mid-market SaaS/revenue platform if a statutory, voluntary, or shareholder-requested audit becomes applicable

stage_6.entry_description: Gross active business income from consumer polling and survey platform services
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-sourced income; foreign-source income is excluded if the company is not NZ tax resident; a CK IC should attach a schedule isolating NZ-source platform revenue.
